sources.decision: TLS, least privilege and replacing demo PKI; do not infer certificate validity from filenames.
TLS and hostname-verification configuration; a snapshot is not a handshake test.
Explicit topology/mapping limits; sizing remains contextual.
Inspect per-item failures, byte bounds, retry and visibility semantics.
Distinguish AWS-managed/serverless service limits from self-hosted OpenSearch controls.
Write-amplification and refresh/merge tuning motivate experiments; five shards, 30s refresh and merge values are not universal rules.
Shard pressure is real; reducing replicas or applying a fixed GB target requires availability/recovery context.
Public preview only of a 2023 first-hand incident account. Used to motivate recovery questions; no paywalled root cause or mitigation details are claimed or admitted.
Separate relevance evaluation from cluster health and ingestion success.
Experiment with byte size, refresh and concurrency; preserve fields needed to identify/retry failed items.
Maintainer chart documentation identifies the unsafe demo-certificate flag and demo-initialization boundary. A false flag is still only configuration evidence, not proof of valid PKI.
